subject: Civil Engineering
title: Wind and Suspension Bridges
description: A fast breakdown of Wind and Suspension Bridges for builders.

hook.text: Suspension bridges are light and flexible — wind is their greatest enemy.

buildup.text: Wind creates vortices that push and pull the deck in rhythmic patterns.

discovery.text: If the vortex frequency matches the bridge's frequency, oscillation amplifies.

twist.text: Aerodynamic deck shapes and wind fairings break up vortices before they grow.

climax.text: The Great Belt Bridge deck was reshaped after wind tunnel tests revealed problems.

punchline.text: Long bridges must be designed as aerodynamic shapes, not flat plates.

quiz.question: How do engineers prevent dangerous wind oscillations in suspension bridges?
options: They add heavy weights to the deck to stop it moving
They shape the deck aerodynamically and add fairings to break up vortices
They limit traffic during windy conditions
